title: Run logs were stamped from the local clock with no zone, while fleet audit renders UTC with a Z
body:
## Summary

A run log was named from the LOCAL clock and carried no zone marker; `fleet audit` renders the same kind of instant in UTC with a trailing `Z`. Two surfaces of one tool, two zones, and only one of them said which.

Measured 2026-09-02:

    $ date    +'%Y%m%d-%H%M local'   ->  20260902-2313 local
    $ date -u +'%Y%m%d-%H%M UTC'     ->  20260902-2213 UTC
    $ ls -t tmp/check/*.SYNTAX.out   ->  tmp/check/20260902-2303.SYNTAX.out

## Why it was not cosmetic

**A stamp with no zone is read as UTC by anyone who has met the whiteboard protocol, and this repository is where that protocol is written down.** The clock guard shipped in `lib/templates/hooks/whiteboard-clock-guard.sh` refuses a commit for exactly this, in three checks. The run logs were the one surface in this tree still doing the thing the guard exists to stop.

**The two surfaces are read side by side.** A reader comparing a `Z`-marked install time from `fleet audit` against a log filename, to ask *was this gate run before or after that re-vendor*, was comparing a UTC instant against an unlabelled local one. In summer the answer is off by an hour in the direction that makes a later run look earlier. Correct in winter and silently wrong in summer is the worst available shape, because the instrument agrees with itself for six months at a time.

## THE BLOCKER THIS ISSUE CITED WAS FALSE, AND IT IS WHY THE ISSUE SAT UNFIXED

This issue argued the fix was *not simply `date -u`*, on the ground that three readers depend on the filename's shape and a zone change would leave one retention window ordered wrongly. **The load-bearing claim was that `newest_run_stems` orders same-minute runs by the time-ordered `-SS` segment. It does not.**

- `newest_run_stems` selection-sorts by **mtime**, via `[ "$f" -nt "$newest" ]`.
- `purge_run_logs` globs on the `*.<suffix>.{out,errors}` SHAPE and never parses the stamp.
- `latest_pointer_keepset` resolves a symlink target.

**All three are zone-agnostic.** The `-SS` rung is a COLLISION device that makes a name unique inside one minute; it was never an ordering device, and this issue conflated the two.

**Driven 2026-09-03 rather than reasoned:** two log files were planted with name order and mtime order deliberately opposed, and `newest_run_stems` returned the older NAME with the newer mtime first.

**`lib/runlog` said so all along, in as many words:** *Ordering is by MTIME, never by name -- same-minute collision files carry a -SS suffix that sorts lexically BEFORE the plain stamp while being newer.* The opposite claim lived in a comment at `bin/devbin`, four hundred lines away, and that is the copy this issue quoted. **Two comments in one repository disagreeing about one function is benign right up until somebody acts on the wrong one** -- here it cost a fix and produced an escalation.

## Fixed

`date -u` at both stamping sites: `bin/devbin` (the invocation stamp) and `lib/runlog` `open_run_log` (the fallback). The seconds rung takes `date -u` too -- seconds are zone-invariant so that is not a correctness change, it is so the whole stamp has one stated provenance and no later reader is invited to restore a local call beside it.

`date +%s` is left alone in three places. Those are EPOCH reads, which carry no zone at all: `DEVBIN_RUN_T0`, the wall-clock delta, and the run id's clock component.

The false comment at `bin/devbin` is replaced with a pointer to the one true home in `lib/runlog`, plus a note of what the duplicate cost.

**Residual, stated rather than left to be found:** for up to `RUNLOG_KEEP_RUNS` (default 5) kept runs, a log directory can show mixed local-stamped and UTC-stamped names. It is cosmetic -- retention and ordering both go through mtime -- and it clears itself within one retention window.

## Test

`tests/unit/runlog.bats`: *the run-log stamp is read from UTC, not the local clock*. Driven under `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` (UTC+14), because under the ambient TZ a local and a UTC stamp are the SAME STRING for half the year and the test would pass against the defect every winter. Asserts both halves: the stamp equals the UTC minute, AND it does not equal the local reading.

**Driven red before being accepted:** with `date -u` reverted to `date` at both sites, it fails with `stamp [20260903-2313] is neither UTC minute [20260903-0913] nor [20260903-0913]` -- the offset, exactly.

## Found

While reading the clock for a board heartbeat and noticing the check log four minutes in the future.
